title: Y1JZ--Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Design-Build & Construction Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) National VA Healthcare Construction Program
description: The VA requires multiple indefinite-delivery, indefinite- quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) type contracts to provide construction services enterprise wide. The objective of this procurement is to award multiple IDIQ MATOCs for construction services nationwide within specified pools. These pools will meet the VA infrastructure needs for construction, renovation, maintenance, and repair within the 50 United States and its territories. title: Office of Space Commerce BPA
description: Description THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY � Solicitations are not available at this time. Requests for a solicitation will not receive a response. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the United States Government and respondents will not be entitled to payment of direct or indirect cost incurred in responding to this request for information (RFI). The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Acquisition and Grants Office (AGO), Corporate Services Acquisition Division (CSAD), located in Silver Spring, MD, is conducting market research to identify businesses and organizations capable of providing specialized space policy research, analysis, consultation, data services, and strategic advisory support. The Government is also seeking information on industry capabilities and approaches for providing flexible, on-demand access to qualified subject matter experts, including short-notice consultations, rapid-turn analyses, and longer-duration support. Responses will help assess the availability of qualified sources, industry capacity to meet varying response timelines, and potential acquisition approaches, including consideration of a multiple-award Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA). NAICS CODE: To be determined Background The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Office of Space Commerce (OSC), is the principal unit for space commerce policy activities within the Department of Commerce. OSC's mission is to foster the conditions for the economic growth and technological advancement of the U.S. commercial space industry. Within OSC, the Policy, Advocacy, and International Division (PAID) supports the development and coordination of domestic and international space commerce policies, promotes U.S. commercial space interests, and engages with government, industry, and international stakeholders on emerging space policy issues. Given the rapidly evolving commercial space environment, PAID requires timely access to specialized expertise, research, data, and analysis to support policy development, strategic planning, and leadership decision-making. These needs may arise with little advance notice and range from brief consultations with subject matter experts to comprehensive research, policy assessments, and longer-duration advisory support. PAID is exploring approaches to obtaining these services that provide flexibility, timely access to qualified experts, and cost-effective support across a broad range of space policy matters. Purpose The purpose of this RFI is to better understand industry capabilities, service delivery approaches, and associated costs and benefits for providing flexible, on-demand space policy research, analysis, consultation, data services, and strategic advisory support. Specifically, the Government seeks information on vendors' demonstrated expertise across the identified Task Areas, their ability to provide timely access to qualified subject matter experts, and their capacity to support both short-duration consultations and more extensive analytical requirements. The Government is also interested in understanding whether these capabilities are available through vendors' existing personnel, established subcontractor or consultant relationships, or other arrangements. Responses will assist OSC in refining its requirements, evaluating potential acquisition and ordering approaches, and determining how best to obtain timely, cost-effective access to specialized expertise. Although this RFI requests specific information, it is not intended to discourage creative thinking on the part of the industry to propose alternative solutions or approaches that the Government may not have considered. Scope and Draft Requirements The attached draft PWS describes seven potential task areas. Respondents may identify one or more areas of demonstrated capability: Commercial Space Policy and Regulation � U.S. commercial space policy, licensing, permitting, regulatory oversight, and interagency issues. Space Traffic Coordination, Safety, and Sustainability � Civil space traffic coordination, SSA, conjunction coordination, debris mitigation, standards and norms. International and Geopolitical Space Policy � International governance, UNCOPUOS, foreign regulatory regimes, geopolitical implications. Space Law and Regulatory Analysis � Domestic/international legal and regulatory research and analysis; not legal representation. Commercial Space Industry and Economic Policy � Commercial space markets, competitiveness, investment, industry data, indicators and economic impacts. Emerging Space Activities and Technology Policy � Policy implications of RPO, in-space servicing, commercial stations, lunar activities, remote sensing and novel services. Strategic and Executive Advisory Support � Expert consultations, executive briefings, workshops, time-sensitive research and decision-support analysis. Potential forms of support include: Consultation Only; Consultation Plus Summary; Research and Analytical Services; Data and Information Services; and Extended Support. Services may be ordered individually or together. The draft PWS describes Rapid (several hours to one business day), Expedited (generally one to two business days), and Standard quotation/availability response categories. These are response expectations, not automatic performance-completion deadlines. The contemplated BPA would have a five-year ordering period, with requirements, schedules, deliverables and pricing established at the individual Call level. The Government has not determined the final acquisition vehicle, number of awards, or ordering procedures. Responses Responses to this RFI must be submitted using the Market Research Questionnaire located at https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdnCIev0vZbNRslzShVW9nCFj-Pe_UgXVdsSmlADasb05Fztg/viewform by Friday, December 8, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. Eastern Time.

title: Depot Intermediate Level and Non-Recurring (DINRE) FY30-34
description: The F-35 Lightning II Joint Program Office (JPO) intends to award a sole-source contract to Lockheed Martin Corporation, Lockheed Martin Aeronautics Company (LM Aero), Fort Worth, Texas, for F-35 non-recurring sustainment support. The scope being procured under the Depot, Intermediate Level, and Non-Recurring Engineering (DINRE) contract includes: Depot Activation; Intermediate-level Maintenance; Sustainment Non-Recurring Engineering Efforts; Reliability, Maintainability, and Health Maturation; Structural Integrity Program and Low Observable Maturation; Structural Integrity Program and Low Observable Maturation; Depot Analysis, Planning, and Implementation; Depot Material Lay-In (MLI); Depot Material Activation; Depot Test Systems Development and Support; eCASS (electronic consolidated automated support system) Repair, Test, and Check; Depot-specific Support Equipment (SE); Maintenance Plan Change (MPC) project opportunities; and organic software maintenance support capabilities. This acquisition is being pursued on a sole-source basis under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) (formerly 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1)), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." LM Aero is the original designer, developer, and manufacturer of the F-35 aircraft and is the only source with the capabilities required to provide sustainment support for F-35 aircraft. LM Aero solely possesses the proprietary design knowledge, technical data rights, and engineering capabilities required to perform this highly specialized work. Because the DINRE contract represents an integrated, highly complex requirement of non-recurring activations and engineering efforts, breaking out individual activation tasks, regional depot lines, or test program sets to alternate vendors is economically and operationally impracticable. Attempting to segregate these tasks would require the Government to duplicate massive, cost-prohibitive systems-engineering overhead and fund redundant tooling. Furthermore, separating technical responsibility across multiple contractors would introduce severe integration risks, void OEM performance warranties, and delay critical organic depot stand-ups, directly degrading fleet-wide mission-capable rates. The DINRE FY30�34 contract is anticipated to be awarded during FY30, supporting the U.S. Services, Cooperative Program Partners, and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) Customers. This notice of intent is neither a request for proposal nor a solicitation of offers. However, in accordance with FAR 5.207(c)(16)(ii), all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation that will be considered by the U.S. Government. Based upon any responses to this notice, the U.S. Government reserves the right to process this procurement action on a sole-source basis. For availability of subcontracting opportunities, contact LM Aero.

Known Authorized Small Business Distributor: LKD Aerospace (CAGE Code: 0CUF4) Single Source / Brand Name Statement: Honeywell is the sole manufacturer of this navigational equipment. Market research indicates LKD Aerospace is currently the only known authorized distributor capable of supplying this stand-alone unit in this region. While the Government intends to solicit and award on a single-source basis to an authorized vendor under RFO 12.102(a), all responsible sources may submit a quotation, which shall be considered by the agency if received by the response deadline. 3. Schedule of Supplies / Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs) - Vendors shall provide firm-fixed-price (FFP) quotations for the following required line items: CLIN 0001 - Part # HG9900C1A-2020 HG9900 IMU, Description: Honeywell HG9900 Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) Quantity: 1 Each CLIN 0002 - Shipping / Freight (F.O.B. Destination to Edwards AFB, CA) 4. Minimum Technical & Salient Characteristics To be considered technically acceptable, the offered unit must strictly meet the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) form, fit, function, and interface specifications: Drift Rate: Maximum drift rate of 0.8 nm/hr. Operating Range: Operational performance rating of �20g. Data Bus Output Protocol: Ability to continuously output Message 3 (TSPI and Built-in Test [BIT] data at 300 Hz). Ability to output Message 4 (Unit serial and temperature data at power-up). Synchronous Data Link Control (SDLC) format with fixed address field configuration compatible with CRIIS flight test hardware. Condition: Factory new / OEM certified. Remanufactured, refurbished, or gray-market items will not be accepted. Must include Certificate of Conformance (CoC) and standard commercial warranty documentation. 5. Delivery and Inspection Details Delivery Date: Required 12 Months After Receipt of Order (ARO). Delivery Terms: F.O.B. Destination. Delivery Location: Air Force Test Center (AFTC), Edwards AFB, CA 93524 Inspection and Acceptance: Destination by the receiving Government representative. 6. Instructions to Offerors (Addenda to FAR 52.212-1) Quotations must be submitted electronically via email to the Contracting Points of Contact listed below no later than the date and time specified. Quote Package Requirements: a. Pricing Schedule: Completed pricing for CLIN 0001 and CLIN 0002. b. Technical Conformance / Authorized Distributor Verification: Proof of OEM authorization to distribute Honeywell IMUs, or documentation verifying OEM origin, traceability, and warranty validation. Specification sheet verifying compliance with part number HG9900C1A-2020 c. Administrative Information: Company Name, Address, and Point of Contact (phone & email). Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code. Business Size status under NAICS 334511. Confirmation of active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov). Quote validity period (minimum 60 calendar days). 7. Evaluation & Basis for Award (Addenda to FAR 52.212-2) & RFO 12.203 The Government will award a Firm-Fixed-Price contract resulting from this solicitation to the offeror whose quote conforms to the solicitation requirements and is determined to be the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA). Factors per RFO 12.203 (a), (b) & (c): a. Technical Acceptability: Quotes will be evaluated on a Pass/Fail basis. To receive a "Pass" rating, the offeror must demonstrate the ability to provide genuine OEM Honeywell HG9900C1A-2020 units meeting all salient characteristics and verified OEM supply-chain provenance. b. Price: Evaluated based on the total firm-fixed-price of CLIN 0001 and CLIN 0002. Price reasonableness will be determined in accordance with RFO Part 12. 203, formerly FAR 13.106-3. c. Quotation(s) and Offer(s). All quotations or offers are to be received by the issued response (due) date and time. 9. Submission Deadline and Contact Information: Quotes Due: 4 Dec 2026, by at 12 PM PST. Quote Submission: Email quotes to the Contract Specialist and Contracting Officer: Terence D. Vickers, NH-III, DAF, terence.vickers@us.af.mil, 6612772232

title: 28th OD Electronics and IED Neutralization Course
description: 1. Introduction & Purpose: The 900th Contracting Battalion (MICC - Fort Bragg, NC) is conducting market research to identify capable sources, specifically looking for Small Businesses (including 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, and HUBZone firms) capable of providing a comprehensive, tactical Electronics and IED Neutralization Course in support of the 28th Ordnance Company (EOD). This is a Sources Sought Notice only and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or Request for Quotation (RFQ). The government will use responses to this notice to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy, specifically whether a socio-economic set-aside is warranted. 2. Core Requirements Summary: The contractor shall provide all personnel, training aids, equipment, facilities, and supervision necessary to execute three (3) five-day courses for up to twelve (12) personnel per iteration (totaling 36 personnel). Key Training Modules: Basic electronics theory, circuit breadboarding, diagnostic tools, and microcontrollers. Advanced hand-entry/defeat techniques under specialized conditions (e.g., Night Vision Goggles / blackout precautions). Improvised Explosive Device (IED) switch diagnostics, radiography, and post-blast diagnostics. Instructor Qualifications: Lead instructors must possess verifiable DoD Special Mission Unit (SMU) EOD operational experience within the last ten (10) years. Facility & Storage Requirements: Dedicated electronics/practical lab workspace to support 12 personnel. Scenario-based tactical training lanes (e.g., multi-building villages or search environments). A secure storage facility of at least 400 sq. ft. for Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) (including NVGs and organic EOD kit) compliant with AR 190-11 (Physical Security of Weapons, Ammunition, and Explosives). Place of Performance: Contractor facility must be located within a 5-hour driving radius of Fort Bragg, NC. Logistics & Accommodations: Government-Furnished: Transportation, student lodging, and meals will be provided by the Government. The contractor is only responsible for training facilities and instruction. 3. Capability Statement Submission Requirements: Interested firms must submit a Capability Statement (not to exceed 5 pages) demonstrating their ability to perform this requirement. Submissions must include: A. Company Profile: Company Name, Address, and Website. Unique Entity ID (UEI) and CAGE Code. Business Size/Socio-Economic Status under NAICS 611699 (e.g., SDVOSB, 8(a), Small Business). B. Technical Capability & Experience: SMU EOD Cadre: Describe your organization's access to and ability to field instructors possessing the required DoD Special Mission Unit (SMU) EOD experience. Facility & Equipment Storage: Describe your facilities, including the practical electronics lab space and tactical scenario lanes. Confirm that your secure storage facility complies with AR 190-11 physical security guidelines. SECTION 2: STATUTORY DISCLAIMER & SPECIAL NOTICE This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes in accordance with FAR 15.101(c). This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an announcement of a forthcoming solicitation. Issuance of this notice does not obligate the Government to issue a formal solicitation or award a contract. The Government will not pay or reimburse any costs incurred by respondents in preparing, submitting, or demonstrating information in response to this notice. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Participation in this RFI is voluntary. Failure to respond will not preclude a vendor from participating in any future competitive acquisition, should one be released. Respondents may submit capability statements addressing any subset or all of the focus areas detailed herein. SECTION 3: BACKGROUND & PROGRAM CONTEXT 3.1 Background & Context Modern surface warfare requires rapid, modular capability delivery across the Navy's surface fleet. The Navy�s ICS program is making this vision a reality through use of virtualization, Kubernetes orchestration, and development of a common suite of mission applications enabling a "build once and deploy across the fleet" methodology for delivery of capability to frigates, destroyers, amphibious ships, aircraft carriers, future manned and unmanned vessels, and future foreign military sales vessels. The ICS program is conducting market research to identify industry partners capable of executing comprehensive systems engineering and software integration for U.S. Navy surface combat systems. This scope is currently being executed under the N00024-23-C-5117 contract awarded to Lockheed Martin Rotary & Mission Systems in September 2023. 3.2 Technical Scope & Baselines The technical scope spans current and next-generation baseline configurations running incremental deliveries of the Integrated Combat System (ICS) software stack (infrastructure services and tactical platform services) and common mission applications. Applicable ship deliveries include the following: ICS-Enabled AEGIS Combat System Baselines 9.C3+ and Baseline 10.1+ running on Mk6 Mod0/1 hardware with IaaS ORDALT or on Mk6 ModX hardware ICS-Enabled Ship Self-Defense System (SSDS) platforms FF(X) 3 and follow DDG 1000 class in line with delivery of the Zumwalt Enterprise Upgrade Solution (ZEUS) Future USN and FMS platforms SECTION 4: TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS & CAPABILITY AREAS SOUGHT The Navy seeks detailed technical capabilities, corporate competencies, and innovative methodologies across eleven (11) functional areas. Vendors may respond to any or all of the following scope areas: Focus Area 1: Programmatic Engineering, Configuration Management & Governance Configuration Management (CM): Formulating, baselining, and executing Configuration Management Plans (CMP), software build/release planning, Configuration Control Boards (CCBs), and tracking and adjudicating Software Change Requests (SWCRs). Programmatic & Systems Planning: Developing, maintaining, and synchronizing project-level Roadmaps, Integrated Master Schedules (IMS), and capability delivery cadences. Focus Area 2: Systems Engineering & Requirements Architecture Technical Baseline Artifacts: Developing, updating, and managing formal engineering artifacts: Systems Engineering Plans (SEP). Software Development Plans (SDP) utilizing modern Agile/DevSecOps frameworks. System / Subsystem Definition Documents (SSDD). System / Subsystem Specifications (SSS). Software Product Specifications (SPS). Interface Requirements Specifications (IRS). Requirements Traceability Verification Matrices (RTVM) maintaining end-to-end bidirectional requirement-to-test traceability. System Safety Plans (SSP) conforming to MIL-STD-882E and naval weapon safety requirements. Requirements Allocation: Decomposing ICS, AEGIS, SSDS, and future combat system Top Level Requirements (TLR) into modular capability building blocks and subsystem specifications across surface ship classes (DDG 51, CG 47, FF(X), DDG 1000, L-Class, CVN, unmanned surface vessels, FMS variants, future platforms). Technical Leadership: Serving as lead technical authorities in Integrated Product Teams (IPTs), Working Groups (WGs), formal milestone reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR), and leading Technical Interchange Meetings (TIMs) to define and allocate interface requirements. Force-Level Mission Thread Analysis: Evaluating complex, distributed kill-chain mission threads, establishing functional allocations, and resolving tactical latency challenges. ICS Re-Architecture & Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE): Authoring SysML/UML MBSE models and leading modular product development across the ICS Domain Architecture. Sensor Management. Vehicle Management. Information Management. Training Management. Tactical Decision Management. External Communications Management. Weapon Management. Display Management. Infrastructure Services. Focus Area 3: Fleet Data Analysis, Feasibility Studies & Gap Assessment Conducting engineering feasibility studies, system performance assessments, and trade studies for capability insertion across diverse ship classes and configurations. Extracting, parsing, and analyzing live fleet exercise data, weapon telemetry, and real-world tactical events to identify performance anomalies and drive capability enhancement. Assessing combat system shortfalls, bottlenecks, and operational gaps, and designing/evaluating candidate architectural and software modifications to close these gaps. Focus Area 4: Tactical Software Design, Coding, Testing, and Integration Combat System Design activities including analysis and algorithm development Mission software development, unit testing, and component integration. Cloud-based and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HWIL)-based testing to include element integration, subsystem testing, and system testing System Integration: Engineering and integrating software interfaces for specific sensor, weapon, and C2 programs and capabilities, including but not limited to: Patriot Advanced Capability-3 Missile Segment Enhancement (PAC-3 MSE) The Standard Missile (SM) Family of weapons (including all Air Defense, Ballistic Missile Defense, and Extended Range Active Missile variants) MK-41 VLS-compatible canister-launched weapons (including Evolved SeaSparrow Missile (ESSM), Tomahawk Land Attack Missile (TLAM), and Vertical Launch ASROC (VLA) Rolling Airframe Missile (RAM) Electronic Warfare (EW) systems Phased array and rotating radar systems Evolving to common track management solution across AEGIS and SSDS configurations Containerized payloads Tactical Virtualization Configurations: Designing, provisioning, benchmarking, and troubleshooting virtualized tactical hardware/software configurations and hypervisor-to-bare-metal runtime environments. Focus Area 5: Hardware/Software Tech Stack, Microservices & System-of-Systems Integration Third-Party Software & Micro

title: Depot Intermediate Level and Non-Recurring Engineering (DINRE) FY30-34
description: The F-35 Lightning II Joint Program Office (JPO) intends to award a sole-source contract to Lockheed Martin Corporation, Lockheed Martin Aeronautics Company (LM Aero), Fort Worth, Texas, for F-35 non-recurring sustainment support. The scope being procured under the Depot, Intermediate Level, and Non-Recurring Engineering (DINRE) contract includes: Depot Activation; Intermediate-level Maintenance; Sustainment Non-Recurring Engineering Efforts; Reliability, Maintainability, and Health Maturation; Structural Integrity Program and Low Observable Maturation; Structural Integrity Program and Low Observable Maturation; Depot Analysis, Planning, and Implementation; Depot Material Lay-In (MLI); Depot Material Activation; Depot Test Systems Development and Support; eCASS (electronic consolidated automated support system) Repair, Test, and Check; Depot-specific Support Equipment (SE); Maintenance Plan Change (MPC) project opportunities; and organic software maintenance support capabilities. This acquisition is being pursued on a sole-source basis under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) (formerly 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1)), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." LM Aero is the original designer, developer, and manufacturer of the F-35 aircraft and is the only source with the capabilities required to provide sustainment support for F-35 aircraft. LM Aero solely possesses the proprietary design knowledge, technical data rights, and engineering capabilities required to perform this highly specialized work. Because the DINRE contract represents an integrated, highly complex requirement of non-recurring activations and engineering efforts, breaking out individual activation tasks, regional depot lines, or test program sets to alternate vendors is economically and operationally impracticable. Attempting to segregate these tasks would require the Government to duplicate massive, cost-prohibitive systems-engineering overhead and fund redundant tooling. Furthermore, separating technical responsibility across multiple contractors would introduce severe integration risks, void OEM performance warranties, and delay critical organic depot stand-ups, directly degrading fleet-wide mission-capable rates. The DINRE FY30�34 contract is anticipated to be awarded during FY30, supporting the U.S. Services, Cooperative Program Partners, and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) Customers. This notice of intent is neither a request for proposal nor a solicitation of offers. However, in accordance with FAR 5.207(c)(16)(ii), all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation that will be considered by the U.S. Government. Based upon any responses to this notice, the U.S. Government reserves the right to process this procurement action on a sole-source basis. For availability of subcontracting opportunities, contact LM Aero.

title: Refurbishment of Existing Tree Cooler, St. Joe Ranger District, Idaho Panhandle National Forests
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 1284LL27Q0008 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) Refurbishment of Existing Tree Cooler. Services and supplies are required for the currently installed tree cooler for the St. Joe Ranger District, Idaho Panhandle National Forests. The tree cooler was built in 1984, the outdated HVAC system shall be replaced with a new HVAC system. The contractor shall provide a fully functioning new HVAC system for the existing tree cooler with associated evaporator fans and necessary materials for the refrigeration system. Contractor shall remove any humidifiers and associated parts, update the lighting, and install a notification system of a power outage due to ongoing power fluctuations. The contractor shall provide the personnel, materials, and equipment needed to perform the required services to industry standards and specifications. Representative shall communicate with POC regarding any issues that may arise. Contractor shall coordinate work hours with CO and COR for site access, hours, and operation. There will be no Government Property issued. Electricity will be available on site for Contractor's use. All work shall be completed by 03/15/2027. See attachment 1284LL27Q0008 for more details. Amendment issued on 11/20/2026, see attachment 1284LL27Q0008_0001 for more information. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 811310 The small business size standard is $12.5 million dollars. This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency.

REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE: All items must meet all requirements of this Statement of Work. The inspection requirements set forth in this SOW shall become part of the contractors overall inspection system or quality program. The absence of any inspection requirements in the SOW shall not relieve the contractor of the responsibility of assuring that all Government equipment submitted for acceptance comply with all requirements. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. REPAIR ASSESSMENT TESTING: The Government may select samples of the Contract Line Items (CLINS) which have completed repair and have been accepted by the Government representative for the purpose of conducting performance testing, environmental testing, and quality conformance examination in a repair assessment test program. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. The historical record file shall include,but not be limited to the following types of historical records: Receipt inspection documentation. Repair shop travelers or repair cards. Parts replacement records. Parts inspection data before and after repair as applicable. Acceptance test data. QA personnel shall maintain a complete receipt inspection,test, repair re-test, history card for each item processed. This information shall be made available to the Government upon request. 4. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. If finished detail drawings are not available, shop drawings in the form used by the manufacturer will be acceptable for Government evaluation. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 3.5 Additive Manufacturing- If/When Additive Manufacturing election taken by vendor, to maintain visibilityover Additively Manufactured components within the supply chain, Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) DD1423 reporting mechanisms apply. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. title: Thomas P. Stafford Building (TPS) Restroom Upgrades at the Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center (MMAC), Oklahoma City, OK
description: *********************THIS IS A MARKET SURVEY ONLY************************* - This is not a Screening Information Request or Request for Proposals of any kind; - The FAA is not seeking or accepting unsolicited proposals; - The FAA will not pay for any information received or costs incurred in preparing the response to the market survey; and - Any costs associated with the market survey submittal are solely at the interested vendor�s expense. - The responses to this market survey will be used for informational purposes only. This is not a Screening Information Request or Request for Proposal of any kind. The FAA is not seeking or accepting proposals at this time. ****************************************************************************** 1. This is a market survey for a construction project titled: Thomas P. Stafford Building (TPS) Restroom Upgrades at the Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center (MMAC), Oklahoma City, OK. 2. The Magnitude of Construction is between $5,000,000 and $10,000,000. Performance and payment bonds will be required in a penal sum equal to 100% of the contract price. The Thomas P. Stafford Building (TPS) at the MMAC is a 222,130 gross square foot building originally constructed in 1991 and is comprised of a basement and two floors above grade. The Thomas P. Stafford Building (Building 27) at the Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center (MMAC) in Oklahoma City functions as a state-of-the-art training complex. It houses the FAA Academy, providing advanced classrooms and simulation laboratories for air traffic control and Technical Operations students and instructors. This project will upgrade the restrooms to meet ADA compliance and will also include upgrades to the corridor finishes. Work associated with construction of this project will be done primarily after hours (Midnight 12:00 am to 6:00 am Monday through Friday) and weekends to prevent disturbance to classes while the building is occupied. The building is fully occupied and runs two shifts of classes from 6:00am to midnight 12:00am Monday through Friday. The work required for the facility will include the following: Provide all labor, equipment, and material to renovate all restrooms on all floors and to upgrade common area finishes in the Thomas P. Stafford building. Requirements will be detailed in the construction plans and specifications provided by the FAA. The project includes: Architectural Restroom Scope: Replace finishes and fixtures in bathrooms on all floors. Replace wall tile, countertops, sinks, faucets, partitions, paint ceilings and doors, new door push plates and kick plates. Provide temporary trailer restrooms to maintain current fixture counts during renovation of restrooms. Only one Men�s and one Women�s restroom in the facility shall be under construction at a time. ADA automatic door openers are to be protected during construction and/or re-installed and operational after renovation at restrooms in which they occur. Mechanical Restroom Scope: Replace supply diffusers and exhaust grilles in restrooms. Fire Sprinkler Scope: Modify fire sprinklers as required. Electrical Restroom Scope: Provide the electrical effort required to upgrade/replace the Lighting and Lighting Controls as part of the coordinated Restroom Upgrades. LD lighting shall be used for both general lighting and egress lighting with footcandle illumination levels meeting both Life Safety required code levels and IES recommended target design levels. Architectural Finishes in Common Circulation Areas Scope: Demo and replace millwork in the Snack Bar area on the first floor. Replace the flooring in the caf�. This work will take place after caf� hours. Flooring replacement to be accomplished over a long weekend and be ready for business opening the following week or at least be in a state to allow normal and sanitary operations of the caf� to continue until work is complete. Corridor walls to full height and gypsum wall board ceilings to receive new high traffic quality paint. The new finish will be applied over the existing Zolatone wall finish and above the existing wall wainscot. Accent color wall paint will be applied to areas as designated in floor plans. Painting can only occur starting Friday at midnight 12:00am but must stop by Saturday at midnight 12:00am (24 hour timeframe) to allow paint odors to dissipate on Sunday. Contractor to provide fans for ventilation to run until Sunday night. Remove circular signage at all doors and paint doors and door frames both sides. Replace with ABA/ANSI A117.1 compliant signage next to doors. Replace walk-off grating at all entrances to the building with walk-off carpeting. VCT (Vinyl Composite Tile) at corridor alcoves to be replaced. Paint all door frames and window framing gray color in place of purple. Painting both sides will require coordination with user groups and will need to be after hours work due to class schedules. Replace stair treads at four exterior staircases, new treads to include an abrasive edge to closely match what is installed at interior atrium staircases. 3. The purpose of this market survey is to solicit statements of interest and capabilities from small businesses, to include applicable small business socio-economic status, capable of providing the required construction services as well as to determine whether adequate competition exists to set-aside the competition among small businesses, to include applicable small business socio-economic status. The NAICS code applicable to this requirement is 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. The business size standard for this NAICS is $45.0 million. The following information shall be provided by interested vendors: 1. Capability Statement - This document should identify: Type of services provided by firm, Vendor�s business size for NAICS code 236220 to include applicable small business socio-economic status Size and type of services provided by previous contracts (provide detailed information and past performance), Number of years in business Evidence of at least one (1) successfully completed construction project greater than $5M in the past five (5) years (provide detailed information and past performance), Respondents must be active in the System for Award Management (SAM) (www.sam.gov). All responses to this market survey must be received by Friday, December 4, 2026, 3:00 p.m. CT. All submittals should be submitted by email to: Lisa.A.Sedlacek-Ewers@faa.gov.

description: Site Access I was hoping you could provide clarity regarding site access. Will a contractor/subcontractor require any kind of badge/permit to gain access to the site and the locations of the dumpsters in addition to regular permits and licenses required for regular operation? A: No badge/ permit is required for the site. The location of the dumpsters is illustrated on page 14 of the solicitation. Technical requirements for submission are listed on page 34. Quantity I want to make sure I m reading the posting correctly. From what I understand you are requesting 12 months x one 6-yard general waste containers emptied weekly 12 months x one 20-yard general waste/headstone/construction materials container emptied monthly with 2 tons monthly included. Estimated annual overage fee for on-call general waste/headstone/construction material containers not expected to exceed 10 tons per year We are performing independent research on the Combined Synopsis/Solicitation (36C78627Q0019). We would like to know if this is a brand-new contract OR if there is (was) an incumbent performing these services. If not brand new, could you please provide the current / previous contract number and what the total contract value was? A: This is a new requirement� CLIN 0001 is priced per month for a "6-yard General waste container emptied weekly," while SOW A.1.1 refers to "the required size and quantity of containers." How many 6-yard containers are required, and are they front-load containers with lids? A: 1 6 yard container. CLIN 0002 describes the 20-yard container as "emptied monthly" (12 EA), while SOW A.1.2 describes on-call, as-needed delivery and pickup within 3 business days. Should offerors price 12 on-call 20-yard hauls per year, and is the 20-yard container kept on site between hauls or delivered only when called? A: the 20 yard container will remain on site and be emptied monthly. Can the Government provide historical tonnage for the 20-yard container (last 12 24 months of weight tickets, total tons and average tons per pull) to support the 2-ton allowance and the 10-ton estimated annual overage? A: Past weight tickets are not available. Is there a Government-recommended landfill or disposal facility for this contract, and are there any special handling requirements for disposing of headstones (e.g., must headstones be broken, defaced or recycled rather than landfilled)? A: The government request is for waste removal services. Disposal of wastes is contractors decision. Headstones will be broken prior to placement in the dumpster. Are concrete landing pads already in place at the 6-yard and 20-yard container locations shown on the site map, and are there any weight limits on cemetery roads for roll-off trucks? A: No. The 6 yard will be in a gravel lot. The 20 yard will go in the spoils lot which is a mix of gravel/dirt. SF1449 Block 8 lists the quote due date as 12-04-2026 at 16:00 EDT, while the SAM.gov notice lists 11:00 AM EST. Which date/time and time zone governs? A: The latest time governs. We would manage the contract and a licensed Indiana hauler would perform the work as our named subcontractor. Will the subcontractor's FMCSA DOT registration and IDEM registration meet the technical requirement? Quoters are strongly encouraged to demonstrate their own relevant experience and capabilities. Reliance on subcontractor experience/ certifications/ licensing to meet these requirements is discouraged and may not be considered sufficient in the evaluation of proposals. Preference will be given to proposals wherein the prime contractor clearly illustrates its direct experience and ability to successfully perform the required work without significant dependence on subcontractor s past performance. Will past performance references from the named subcontractor be accepted? Quoters are strongly encouraged to demonstrate their own relevant experience and capabilities. Reliance on subcontractor experience/ certifications/ licensing to meet these requirements is discouraged and may not be considered sufficient in the evaluation of proposals. Preference will be given to proposals wherein the prime contractor clearly illustrates its direct experience and ability to successfully perform the required work without significant dependence on subcontractor s past performance. The RFQ refers to an "IDEM license." Which IDEM registration or permit number should the quote show for a solid waste hauler? A: License to provide services in accordance with: https://www.in.gov/idem/waste/resources/permits-registrations-approvals-and-closures/ Does VAAR 852.219-75 apply, given that the RFQ is unrestricted? 852.219-75 does not apply, however the technical factor of the prime contractor clearly illustrates its direct experience and ability to successfully perform the required work without significant dependence on subcontractor s past performance does apply. How many 6-yard containers are required? The CLIN says "container" and the SOW says "containers at each active site." A: 1 container Could you share the current contract number for this service? A: No current contract Technical acceptability (Volume B). Section E.3 (FAR 52.212-2) establishes award on a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable basis, with Technical Acceptability as a pass/fail factor, but the solicitation does not list the elements that make a quotation technically acceptable. Could you confirm the specific minimum requirements the Government will evaluate, and whether a Volume B technical response is required in addition to the Volume A administrative documents described in the Instructions to Quoters? A: Technical acceptability is listed on page 34. Quoter shall include the following in Volume B in accordance with the Technical Qualifications criteria listed in the Evaluation Process section of this combined synopsis solicitation: Provide management plans in a clear, definitive process for how the contractor intends to complete all the work as outlined in the statement of work to include vehicles required to perform the work. Provide proof of at least 1 year experience in trash collection, of similar Size (size of the cemetery), scope (cemetery work and interments) and complexity. DOT registered vehicles required to perform services as verifiable by https://safer.fmcsa.dot.gov/CompanySnapshot.aspx License to provide services in accordance with: https://www.in.gov/idem/waste/resources/permits-registrations-approvals-and-closures/ Tonnage basis for CLIN 0003 (overage). CLIN 0002 states that 2 tons are included with the monthly 20-yard container service, and CLIN 0003 prices estimated annual overage beyond 2 tons. Is the 2-ton allowance applied per container per month or per collection? Also, how will tonnage be documented and invoiced for example, by landfill scale tickets submitted with each invoice? title: FCI Leavenworth Elevator & Chairlift Maintenance Requirement
description: ELEVATOR AND CHAIRLIFT MAINTENANCE SERVICES FCI LEAVENWORTH Category: Facilities, Subcategory: Facilities Maintenance and Repair NAICS: 561210 1. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The Federal Bureau of Prisons, Federal Correctional Institution Leavenworth, requests quotations from eligible contractors for elevator and chairlift maintenance services in accordance with the attached Statement of Work. The requirement covers: - One traction elevator serving the Administrative Building. - One hydraulic elevator serving the Food Service/West Storeroom. - One Garaventa GSL Artira chairlift serving the Administrative Building entrance. Services include quarterly preventive maintenance, scheduled and unscheduled repairs, emergency callback services, service reporting, and annual inspection support as specified in the final SOW. The Government anticipates issuing one firm-fixed-price task order with a 12-month base period and four 12-month option periods. Place of Performance: FCI Leavenworth 1300 Metropolitan Avenue Leavenworth, Kansas 66048 Period of Performance - Base Period: January 1, 2027 - December 31, 2027 Option Year 1: January 1, 2028 - December 31, 2028 Option Year 2: January 1, 2029 - December 31, 2029 Option Year 3: January 1, 2030 - December 31, 2030 Option Year 4: January 1, 2031 - December 31, 2031 2. QUOTATION SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Submit quotations by the closing date and time identified in this RFQ to Contract Specialist, Kathleen Wood, kwood1@bop.gov. Quotations must include the following: A. Contractor Information Provide: - Legal business name, business address, and UEI. - Point of contact, telephone number, and email address. - Quotation validity period. - Acknowledgment of all solicitation amendments. B. Technical Service Approach Submit a technical service approach of no more than three pages addressing: 1. Equipment capability: Explain the ability to maintain and repair the traction elevator, hydraulic elevator, and Garaventa chairlift identified in the SOW. 2. Maintenance and inspection support: Describe the approach to quarterly preventive maintenance, service scheduling, reporting, and annual inspection support. 3. Staffing continuity: Describe qualified primary and backup technician coverage, availability during absences or concurrent service calls, and any subcontracting arrangements. 4. Emergency response: Explain the dispatch arrangements and available resources supporting the SOW's one-hour response requirement for trapped individuals and two-hour response requirement for other outages. 5. Parts and technical support: Explain access to necessary replacement parts, diagnostic tools, and technical support. 6. Institution coordination: Explain coordination of technician approvals, backup personnel, institution entry, escorts, tool control, and service scheduling. Provide a practical explanation of how the services will be performed. A general statement agreeing to comply with the SOW does not adequately describe the proposed approach. C. Past Performance: Provide up to three examples of similar services performed within the past five years, including ongoing work. Government, commercial, and relevant subcontract performance may be submitted. For each example, provide: - Customer and project name. - Contract or order number, if available. - Performance dates. - Equipment and services covered. - Contractor's role. - Relevant performance results, including service reliability, emergency response, and resolution of performance problems. - Customer reference name, business email, and telephone number. Limit each example to one page. Contractors without relevant past performance should state that fact. D. Pricing: Complete the pricing schedule below for the base period and all four option periods. Provide one annual firm-fixed price for each period covering all three units and all services included in the final SOW. Include all necessary labor, supervision, equipment, tools, travel, reporting, included repairs and parts, emergency callbacks, and inspection support. Identify any exceptions or proposed exclusions. Do not assume that contractor standard service-agreement exclusions apply. - Base Period: - Option Year 1: - Option Year 2: - Option Year 3: - Option Year 4: - E. Page Limits The three-page technical limit excludes contractor identification, past-performance examples, pricing, required representations, amendment acknowledgments, and exceptions. Use readable text of at least 11 points on standard letter-size pages. Technical pages exceeding the three-page limit will not be evaluated. Do not place additional technical narrative in excluded sections to circumvent the limit. 3. EVALUATION AND BASIS FOR SELECTION The Government will select the eligible Schedule contractor whose quotation meets the solicitation requirements and provides the best value considering: 1. Technical Service Approach. 2. Past Performance. 3. Price. Technical Service Approach is more important than Past Performance. Together, the nonprice factors are more important than Price. A. Technical Service Approach The Government will evaluate how well the proposed approach demonstrates the ability to maintain the identified equipment and meet the SOW. Considerations include equipment familiarity; maintenance and inspection-support planning; qualified primary and backup staffing; credible emergency dispatch and response coverage; access to parts and diagnostic support; and coordination with institution access requirements. These considerations explain the technical factor and are not separately weighted subfactors. B. Past Performance The Government will evaluate the relevance and quality of available past-performance information, including maintenance reliability, emergency response, and resolution of service problems. The Government may obtain information from submitted references, CPARS where applicable, and other available sources. A contractor without relevant past performance, or for whom sufficient information is unavailable, will not be evaluated favorably or unfavorably solely because of that absence. C. Price The Government will evaluate the sum of the base-period price and all four option-period prices. All quotations must address the same final SOW requirements. Evaluation of options does not obligate the Government to exercise them. D. Comparative Evaluation The Government will compare quotations directly against the stated evaluation factors and one another to identify meaningful differences and determine which quotation provides the best value. Numerical scores and adjectival ratings will not be assigned. The selection will be supported by a narrative explaining the material differences and their importance to successful performance. The Government may select a higher-priced quotation when its benefits warrant the additional price. The Government may select a lower-priced quotation when additional benefits do not justify a higher price. The Government intends to make its selection based on initial quotations but may communicate with contractors or request revised quotations when appropriate. Contractors should submit their best technical and pricing terms initially. 4. SITE VISIT Date and Time: December 1, 2026 at 10:00 AM Registration Deadline: November 25, 2026 at 3:00 PM Reporting Location: FCI Leavenworth, 1300 Metropolitan Ave. Leavenworth, KS 66048 A. Purpose and Attendance The Government will conduct a site visit to allow prospective quoters to observe the covered equipment and become familiar with the service locations, equipment conditions, and institution access requirements. Attendance is encouraged but is not mandatory and will not be evaluated as a condition of award. Contractors remain responsible for submitting quotations addressing the entire solicitation and SOW. title: FCI Oxford - Water Softener
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) and the Federal Correctional Institution Oxford located at 350 Elk Avenue, Oxford, Wisconsin, intend to make a single award to a responsible entity that will provide all necessary equipment, labor, materials, and incidentals to remove existing water softeners and install a new centralized water softener for the entire Institution. Awarded Contractor shall provide materials, labor, and equipment to remove existing water softeners, pipe through and install a new centralized water softener and all associated components. FCI Oxford currently has several commercial-grade water softeners which are failing to efficiently reduce water hardness and protect water systems, as well as connected equipment. The new centralized system should improve water quality, minimize calcium buildup, and extend the service life of plumbing infrastructure and appliances. The contractor would place a brine tank and softener to be installed at the water tower. Water would be treated right off the water main, therefore there would be no need for bagged salt to be brought in weekly.

title: MORIAH WIND SYSTEM (MWS)
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION - SOURCES SOUGHT NAVAL AIR WARFARE CENTER, AIRCRAFT DIVISION LAKEHURST, NJ MORIAH WIND SYSTEM (MWS) THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ONLY. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued pursuant to FAR 15.201(e). This RFI is for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation or promise to issue a solicitation in the future. It is a Market Research tool being used to identify potential technologies and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWC-AD) Lakehurst is seeking to continue the production of the U.S. Fleet wind systems for program management, production, systems engineering, logistics support and acceptance for the Moriah Wind System (MWS). The MWS program produces multiple configurations and variants of the MWS and associated components. A description of the Moriah Wind System follows: MWS provides digital wind speed and direction information, including crosswind and headwind, that supports decision making for air operations, combat, navigation, tactical planning and firefighting. The MWS replaces legacy Type F Wind Measuring and Indicating and Digital Wind Systems (DWS), providing a single wind measuring system, consistent across all ship classes, Land Based Test Site, and shore stations. MWS consists of the following main parts: Ultrasonic Wind Sensor Unit (WSU) with non-moving parts Wind Processor unit (WPU) consisting of dual redundant processors capable of interfacing with legacy wind and ship systems and Shipboard Local Area Networks (LANs) High-End Display (HED) with full range of available wind information and ship speed/ course data, including the display of Aircraft Recovery Bulletins (ARBs), Launch and Recovery Envelopes (LREs) and Final Course data. The HED is hardwired to one of the WSUs in a safety critical configuration to enable the display of wind data when the WPU or another connecting network is not functioning. HED fits inside an envelope no larger than11.50� high by 18.00� wide by 9.53� deep. This does not include maintenance access, connector access or environmental excursions. HED must be NVD compatible. Low-End Display (LED) with basic wind information and ship speed/course data. LED fits inside an envelope no larger than 7.36� high by 11.10� wide by 6.06� deep. This does not include maintenance access, connector access or environmental excursions. LED must be NVD compatible. The Air Temperature and Humidity Sensor (ATHU) is an accurate self-contained instrument for measuring external air temperature and humidity. The sensor electronics are enclosed in ruggedized stainless-steel housing. The Air Pressure Unit (APU) is an accurate self-contained instrument for measuring external air pressure. The sensor element and all associated electronics to produce a unidirectional serial data interface are housed in a cast aluminum box. The WSUs, HEDs and LEDs are uniform across ship classes, land-based test sites, and shore stations, with the quantity of each item dependent upon ship class/shore location. Every MWS has one WPU with dual-redundant processors, which will differ depending upon ship class and shore station either of which can individually perform all the functions necessary to keep MWS running. The sub-processors communicate with each other directly and periodically to determine functional status and to allow changes in control when a failure is detected. MWS accesses unclassified data only. There is a degree of system-to-system information exchange in MWS. Neither MWS nor its components are connected to the Global Information Grid (GIG). MWS data is output from its WPU in several ways: 1) synchro interfaces to provide wind information to legacy systems (SLQ-32, SPN-46, Integrated Launch and Recovery Television System (ILARTS), and Arresting Gear Crosscheck System); 2) serial and network interfaces for output of wind, navigational and system information to displays; and 3) network interfaces to communicate wind information to other ship systems and MWS displays. Currently, MWS will communicate over Aviation Data Management and Control System (ADMACS) on CVNs, through Digital Multiplex System (DMS) on DDGs and on a MWS controlled network on all other ship classes. Wind data is transmitted in the standard message format and protocol (SMF&P) data format and the National Marine Electronics Association (NMEA) data format. MWS receives the ARBs it displays through ADMACS via Network File System (NFS). MWS displays LREs that are programmed into the HEDs. In order to display ship�s speed and direction, calculate true wind speed and direction, as well as pitch and roll, MWS receives a data packet from Navigation Sensor System Interface (NAVSSI), which contains a host of navigational data, including ship�s positional information. MWS does not use any of this other information, although it must read the entire NAVSSI data packet prior to extracting the data required. The information in this packet is not sensitive unless the information is transmitted off the ship. However, MWS has no mechanism for transmitting data off the ship, nor any requirement to do so. MWS uses strictly defined data types for transmission into and out of the system. This information is limited to either NMEA ASCII strings using checksums to determine data integrity, structured binary data format using checksums to determine data integrity, proprietary DMS Light Internet Protocol (DLIP), and analog synchro resolver output to other ship systems. The data items themselves are confined to information from known systems (as defined in the relevant Interface Requirements Specifications) or is confined to IP addresses and ports specified in the Interface Design Documents (IDD) and the network architecture (ADMACS, DMS or other ship network). The components contain no TELNET or File Transfer Protocol (FTP) capability. Configuration is done via a manual procedure where a MWS cyber accredited laptop is attached to the system components using a serial cable (RS-422) and programming is done via contractor supplied software applications. The processor software was written to run under a tailored Linux Operating System with minimal functionality on an Intel/ARM platform. This operating system consists of a Linux kernel that has been built specifically for use in this environment that will aid security. It contains only those device drivers and services that are relevant to this embedded environment. Software design protects system integrity by the fact that unauthorized personnel do not have the ability to modify the software configuration, data or application. MWS is not designed for use or visibility on the internet and there is no access to the internet. MWS uses UDP/IP & TCP/IP for unicast and multicast communication protocols. NAWC-AD Lakehurst is requesting information from industry for the purpose of identifying qualified contractors interested in producing MWS. The objective of this is to continue production of the following MWS parts, which establish the current MWS configuration baseline: P/N Nomenclature P/N 81164/0200.00 Wind Sensor Unit (WSU) P/N 82374-0200-00 Wind Sensor Unit (WSU) P/N 81161/0200.00/E High End Display (HED) P/N 82371-0200-00-E High End Display (HED) P/N 81162/0200.00/E Low End Display (LED) P/N 82372-0200-00-E Low End Display (LED) P/N 81161/0102.00 HED LED GUI KIT P/N 82371-0102-00 HED LED GUI KIT P/N 81163/0102.00 WPU GUI KIT P/N 81163/0200.00W01 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V1 P/N 82373-0200-00W01 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V1 P/N 81163/0200.00W04 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V3 P/N 82373-0200-00W04 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V3 P/N 81163/0200.00W05 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V5 P/N 81163/0200.00W06 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V6 P/N 82373-0200-00W07 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V7 P/N PS753 28 VDC Power Supply P/N 81163/0300.00W04 WPU Sub-Processor Unit (SPU) Fiber-optic P/N 82

title: Request for Information (RFI): Aerosol Robotic Network (AERONET) Project
description: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) is hereby soliciting information from potential sources for sun/sky/lunar scanning photometers and replacement parts in support of the Aerosol Robotic Network (AERONET) in the Earth Sciences Division (ESD) at NASA/GSFC. AERONET is a global network of ground-based sun and sky-scanning radiometers that measures aerosol optical properties and precipitable water in near real time. NASA uses AERONET data to validate satellite aerosol retrievals and to maintain a uniform long-term record of aerosol properties. AERONET's installed base is more than 600 CE318-series photometers at land, ocean, and ship sites worldwide. The value of the network depends on standardized measurement, calibration, data format, and processing across every site. Any instrument added to the network must produce data that can be merged into the AERONET record and must work with the network's existing site infrastructure, including its tracking robots. The Government requires a contractor to supply both new sun/sky/lunar scanning photometers and replacement parts for the fielded fleet. New instruments are required in standard, polarization, and ocean-color configurations. They must automatically measure direct sun and lunar irradiance and diffuse sky radiance from 340 to 1640 nm; achieve a signal-to-noise ratio above 10,000:1 on all channels; transmit data through the NOAA/NESDIS Data Collection System (DCS), worldwide 4G/5G cellular networks, and PC/internet; run unattended on battery and 5-watt solar power; and operate sealed against rain, humidity, dust, and smoke from -20 to 50 degrees C. Replacement parts, such as sensor head cards, detectors, filters, collimators, CPU cards, modems, robot hardware, and gear reducer motor assemblies, must fit and work in NASA's fielded CE318-series instruments. NASA/GSFC is seeking capability statements from U.S. VENDORS ONLY, for the purposes of determining the appropriate acquisition strategy and level of competition for this requirement. For this RFI, a U.S. vendor is a firm organized under the laws of the United States or a U.S. state, with its principal place of business in the United States. NASA welcomes responses from U.S. manufacturers, authorized U.S. distributors, and other U.S. firms, including all socioeconomic categories of small business. Capability statements from foreign firms will not be reviewed. The Government reserves the right to consider a Small, 8(a), Women-owned (WOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned (SDVOSB), Economically Disadvantaged Women-owned Small Business (EDWOSB), or HUBZone business set-aside based on responses received. Interested firms that possess the capability to meet the above requirement as described in the attached Statement of Work (SOW) are encouraged to submit a capability statement indicating the ability to meet all aspects of the requirement. NASA seeks input in the following areas: 1. Whether your firm is the manufacturer, an authorized distributor, or a reseller. Identify the manufacturer and country of manufacture for each item you would supply. 2. How your instruments meet the measurement, performance, communication, power, and environmental requirements in the SOW. If your instrument is not a CE318-series unit, explain how it would produce data compatible with the AERONET record, for example through side-by-side intercalibration results or use in AERONET or a similar federated network. 3. How your firm would supply replacement parts that fit and work in the fielded CE318-series units. 4. Your firm's experience supplying similar instruments or parts to government, research, or commercial customers in the past five years, with contract numbers and customer contacts. 5. Whether the items are commercial products as defined in FAR 2.101, and any applicable GSA Schedule or other government-wide contract vehicle. 6. Any requirement in the SOW that you believe unnecessarily limits competition, and what you would recommend instead. Each capability statement should also include the firm's name, address, Unique Entity ID (UEI), CAGE code, SAM.gov registration status, business size and socioeconomic status under NAICS 334516, and a point of contact with name, title, phone, and email. title: Code 08 Financial Support Services
description: The Office of Naval Research (ONR) Comptroller Directorate (Code 08) requires contractor support to provide comprehensive financial management, accounting reconciliation, and administrative support services in support of Budget Submitting Office 14 (BSO 14). Support encompasses budget execution, accounting research, and fiduciary reporting for the Department of the Navy (DON) Science and Technology (S and T) and Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation (RDT and E) appropriations across the three Code 08 divisions: Execution/Fiscal Control, Accounting, and Operations/Financial Management. Key requirements include resolving unmatched transactions (UMTs) in Navy ERP, performing unliquidated obligation (ULO) reviews utilizing the Smart Tri-Annual Tool (STAT), compiling Key Supporting Documentation (KSD) for audit readiness, and managing financial record archiving and front-office operations on-site at ONR Headquarters in Arlington, VA.
